zh: 现款自运批发商店；付现自运批发
en: a large wholesale shop that sells goods in large quantities at low prices to customers from other businesses who pay in cash and take the goods away themselves; the system of buying and selling goods in this way

zh: （婚礼、聚会等场合的）售饮料柜台
en: a bar at a wedding, party, etc., at which the guests have to pay for their own drinks rather than getting them free
a box with a lock for keeping money in, usually made of metal
ex: The cash box was kept in the safe at the back of the shop.
现金箱放在商店后部的保险柜。

en: a plastic card used to get money from a cash machine (= a machine in or outside a bank)

zh: 金牛，摇钱树，赢利部门（一企业中始终赢利并给其他部门提供资金的部门）
en: the part of a business that always makes a profit and that provides money for the rest of the business
a crop grown for selling, rather than for use by the person who grows it
ex: Most farmers now produce cash crops such as coffee and tobacco for the export market.
现在大多数农民种植咖啡、烟草之类供出口的经济作物。

en: the place in a shop where you pay for goods that you have bought
ex: She paid for the book at the cash desk.
她在收银台付了书钱。

en: a machine in or outside a bank, shop, etc., from which you can get money from your bank account using a special plastic card
the movement of money into and out of a business as goods are bought and sold
ex: a healthy cash flow (= having enough money to make payments when necessary)
良好的资金周转状况

zh: the name given to events in 1996 when some conservative Members of Parliament were accused of accepting money from business people in order to ask questions for them in Parliament. The 'cash for questions affair' was one of the reasons why the Conservatives were so badly defeated in the 1997 general election.
en: the name given to events in 1996 when some conservative Members of Parliament were accused of accepting money from business people in order to ask questions for them in Parliament. The 'cash for questions affair' was one of the reasons why the Conservatives were so badly defeated in the 1997 general election.

zh: 把（保险单等）提前兑成现金
en: to gain an advantage for yourself from a situation, especially in a way that other people think is wrong
ex: The film studio is being accused of cashing in on the singer's death.
那家电影制片厂被指责利用这位歌手的死来赚钱。
